RELABELLED from GI.P2: Supplemental Table 1 lists this strain under GI.P2, but Table 2 of the same paper designates AJ606693 as GI.4[P1], i.e. P-type GI.P1. The sequence data agree: its RdRp is 0.272-0.281 from the GI.P2 references and 0.144 from GI.P1, and moving it returns GI.P2's within-type maximum from 0.281 to 0.035, inside the published 0-0.119 range.

RELABELLED from GI.P5: Supplemental Table 1's RdRp block has NO GI.P6 row at all, jumping GI.P5 to GI.P7, and lists five strains under GI.P5. Table 2 of the same paper designates MG012443 as GI.6[P6], i.e. P-type GI.P6, so GI.P6 exists in the scheme and its block was dropped from the supplement, its members falling under GI.P5. Four independent lines agree on where the boundary lies. The RdRp distances split the five into two tight clusters, DQ366345 + LC504396 at 0.050 and LC380411 + MG012443 + MN509083 at 0.019-0.057, which are 0.249-0.255 apart. The published GI.P5 range of 0-0.052 matches the first cluster exactly and is impossible for all five, whose spread is 0.255. The VP1 genotypes partition on the same line: GI.5 for the first cluster, GI.6 for the second. And Table 2's GI.P5 representative, DQ366345, sits in the first. So the second cluster is GI.P6. GI.P6's own published range is left NA because the supplement gives no row for it.

RELABELLED from GNA2.P: Supplemental Table 1's RdRp block pairs GNA2.P with OQ818319 and GNA3.P with OP963623, crossing the VP1 block, which assigns GNA2 to OP963623 and GNA3 to OQ818319. The paper's pig/bat table gives the uncrossed pairing for both strains. Two lines of evidence favour the pig/bat table. First, all 18 other VP1/RdRp group discordances in the supplement place a strain in a PRE-EXISTING P-group, which is what recombination looks like; these two are the only ones naming a P-group coined in this same paper, and a de novo GNA2.P has no source for its label other than the capsid genogroup of its own strain, OP963623. Second, each strain is the only member of its P-group, so a reciprocal swap leaves every pairwise distance unchanged and cannot be detected or refuted from the sequence data; the published tables are the only evidence, and they are 1-1 against the supplement here.

RELABELLED from GNA4.P: Supplemental Table 1 assigns this strain GNA4/GNA4.P, but the paper's pig/bat table gives GXV/GXV.P, and GXV/GXV.P is the assignment confirmed manually against the published tables by A. Fitzpatrick (2026-11-17). We follow that. This supersedes an earlier decision here to keep GNA4 on the argument that a name coined in the paper cannot be empty: that inference is outweighed by a direct reading of the tables. The consequence is that GNA4 and GNA4.P have no members, GXV gains a second strain alongside MF175077, and GXV.P a second alongside MF175077.
